rv.q: Absolute Hell is bold and ambitious, fascinating and provocative.
It’s a lot of fun to watch: we love seeing other people behaving terribly, after all, and set in an anything-goes Soho, this lot are deliciously bad.
Director Joe Hill-Gibbins' production is a deliberately slow-burn, but the three hours it takes are captivatingly detailed.

It is a world perfectly depicted in Lizzie Clachan’s crumbling set, yet the production fails to get to the heart of Ackland’s script, relying too much on gimmicks to distract the audience from the text. Aaron Heffernan (Butch) and Kate Fleetwood (Christine) in Absolute Hell.
After a while, it is difficult to feel much sympathy.
